newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on US dlr's Asia correction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on US dlr's Asia correction.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed fairly higher against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, mainly reflecting the greenback's downward correction in Asian markets, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at T$27.490 to the U.S. dollar, against Wednesday's T$27.523 close. Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$328 million.
The Taiwan dollar rose right from the opening as the U.S. dollar faded in Tokyo and elsewhere, then stabilised.
"Since then the Taiwan dollar had been trading narrowly at this higher level," said one dealer.

"During trading some foreign funds had flowed in to strengthen the upward momentum (by the Taiwan dollar), but some U.S. dollar demand linked to oil imports also appeared to slightly offset the uptrend," another dealer said.
Dealers said the market was insensitive to Thursday's release of October trade data showing a US$532 million surplus that nevertheless was 62.2 percent smaller than Taiwan's October 1995 surplus.
"A shrunken trade surplus tends to push down the Taiwan dollar, but the market simply did not react to it. Maybe some had already expected it," said one dealer.
For Friday, a range of T$27.48-27.52 was seen.
